items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I remember it was '33 or '34. I went back the next year, they had those long trailers and he was the first person to put thousands of dollars in a big trailer... I heard at that time that he paid his men $75 a week

ctx.x: Sioux City. Now we worked -- the agency used to be Tom Archer, and I still think he might be alive or some of his relatives -- Tom Archer. He used to hire the territorial bands, and he used to have a whole string of ballrooms, some of them were out in the prairie; Sioux City, Iowa, Sioux Falls, Pipestone, Minnesota and Kansas City, which I'll get to -- we haven't got there yet -- and Lincoln, Nebraska, we had to play in a sandstorm.

This Tom Archer -- his ace in the whole was a six-piece orchestra and was called Lawrence Welk, doing one nighters -- 7 one nighters a week, and they made hundreds and hundreds of thousands of dollars; they were sold out playing polkas, and we would follow them with our appetizing 13 or 14-piece hokum band, they used to call them in those days.
Now what year is this? We just mentioned Boston in 1933 -- is this still ...
